name: What bathroom layout changes require a permit in Los Angeles?

mainEntity.name: What bathroom layout changes require a permit in Los Angeles if I move plumbing, add a shower, or change a wall?
mainEntity.text: What bathroom layout changes require a permit in Los Angeles if I move plumbing, add a shower, or change a wall?

acceptedAnswer.text: If the bathroom layout changes involve moving plumbing, changing wall locations, opening up a bathroom, or adding new electrical or plumbing points in a wall, the project usually needs a fuller permit review rather than a basic fixture-replacement permit. Homeowners should expect to submit an existing floor plan and a proposed floor plan, especially when walls or openings change. The safest approach is to confirm the scope before demolition starts, because layout changes can affect inspection timing, plumbing rough-in, and final sign-off. For Los Angeles-area homes, the difference between a cosmetic remodel and a layout change matters a lot for both schedule and cost. A contractor should be able to tell you whether the work stays within a simple replacement scope or needs a more detailed approval path.
acceptedAnswer.description: In Los Angeles, simple fixture replacement may qualify for a limited permit, but changing walls, openings, or adding new plumbing or electrical locations usually requires plan check and approved permits. A layout change that moves a toilet, shower, vanity, or door opening is typically treated as a more involved remodel than a same-location refresh.
